UnitStatement: DEL-02-04 is the deliverable Toolkit Options and Local UI State.
DEL-02-04 belongs to PKG-02, Desktop Shell, Navigation, and Operator State.
DEL-02-04 uses the SOFTWARE_DECOMP decomposition variant at revision v3.2.
DEL-02-04 is typed as a UX_UI_SLICE with context envelope S.
DEL-02-04 covers scope items SOW-004, SOW-008, and SOW-016 and maps to objectives OBJ-001 and OBJ-004.
ResponsibleParty for DEL-02-04 is TBD.
Primary UI surfaces are the File Tree, Toolkit, and Chat panes for layout behavior, with the Toolkit panel for runtime options.
The Toolkit exposes runtime option categories: model, tools, max turns, mode, persona, and governance metadata as supported by runtime.
Model, tools, and max-turn options follow deterministic fallback chains.
Unknown option keys are ignored with warnings.
Toolkit settings, pane widths, chat drafts, attachment selections, and local presets are local convenience state.
Keyboard users can resize and collapse panes; resize handles are focusable separators with arrow, Home, and End behavior.
Local UI state is non-authoritative and must not override governance enforcement or project truth.
Agent outputs and UI/runtime state remain draft or decision-support material until accepted by an accountable human.
Storage failures for chat drafts and attachment selections warn without breaking chat.
Malformed draft or attachment records are dropped.
Toolkit mode controls must map to permission policy modes once the policy engine exists.
PRD source is usable with warning: _REFERENCES.md REF-006 reports an expected PRD SHA differing from the observed SHA.
Toolkit controls are UI controls for per-turn runtime options supported by the runtime; exact component names and implementation files are TBD.
Pane state controls provide drag and keyboard resize/collapse support for File Tree, Toolkit, and Chat panes with locally persisted widths.
Draft and preset guards use local persistence keyed per root/persona/mode; malformed records are dropped and storage failures warn.
Local presets and option visibility cannot become authoritative or override runtime governance.
Runtime option keys follow accepted fallback behavior; unknown keys warn and do not silently mutate behavior.
References cite docs/DIRECTIVE.md, docs/CONTRACT.md (invariants K-NOMEM-1, K-SDK-1, K-PERM-3, K-TOOL-1), docs/SPEC.md, docs/TYPES.md, docs/PRD.md, and SOFTWARE_DECOMP v3.2.
DEL-02-04 exists to make runtime options and local operator conveniences visible and usable without turning those conveniences into project truth.
DEL-02-04 supports OBJ-001 by preserving clear desktop-shell operator behavior and supports OBJ-004 where Toolkit options touch deterministic runtime option handling.
Principle: treat local state as convenience, not authority; UI drafts, presets, pane widths, transcripts, API keys, logs, and caches are non-authoritative unless governed files import them.
Principle: keep governance stronger than UI choice; Toolkit settings and options express operator intent but cannot override governance enforcement, permission policy, or project truth.
Principle: prefer explicit warnings over silent behavior changes; unknown option keys warn and are ignored, and storage failures warn without breaking chat.
Principle: preserve drafts for operator continuity, not approval; draft and attachment-selection persistence aids recovery but does not approve work or create project truth.
Principle: make pane controls accessible; resize/collapse affordances should be usable by keyboard users through focusable separators and keyboard behavior.
Runtime option controls should distinguish operator-selected, runtime-defaulted, and governance-enforced states where the source model supports it; exact UI copy and state model are TBD.
Local storage should degrade gracefully; blocked quota, private-window limits, or parse errors should not make chat unusable, malformed records are dropped, and failures warn.
The Toolkit should not imply SDK or permission modes are prompt hints only; PRD FR-044 requires runtime enforcement once the permission policy engine exists.
PRD FR-006 points to docs/ui/UI_POLISH_EXECUTION_PLAN.md for polish acceptance, but that file was not accessible; dense professional interface review is required with checklist location TBD.
Trade-off: persist pane widths, drafts, and presets locally, but never write them as authoritative deliverable state unless a governed import occurs.
Trade-off: surface Toolkit options that improve operator control, but let runtime fallback, validation, and permission policy remain authoritative.
Trade-off: drop malformed local records and warn on storage failures, but avoid breaking chat when local persistence fails.
Trade-off: keep resize/collapse controls keyboard-accessible even in a dense desktop shell layout.
Example: a user adjusts Toolkit max turns for one turn; the UI may submit the option but runtime fallback and policy decide final behavior.
Example: when a malformed local draft record is encountered, the UI drops it and continues with a warning if needed.
Example: pane widths persist locally after keyboard resize.
Counter-example: a local Toolkit preset that attempts to bypass governance or override permission policy is unsupported as project truth.

Step: confirm scope boundaries, including Toolkit controls, pane resize/collapse state, local draft/preset guards, and UI handling of runtime option fallback, excluding runtime engine internals and DEL-02-05 API key/error-feedback UI.

Step: implement or review pane resize/collapse behavior for File Tree, Toolkit, and Chat panes, supporting drag and keyboard behavior including Home collapse and End expand, and persisting widths locally.

Step: implement or review Toolkit per-turn option controls exposing model, tools, max turns, mode, persona, and governance metadata only as supported by runtime, recording the supported inventory or marking unavailable controls TBD/disabled.

Step: align Toolkit option handoff with deterministic runtime behavior, confirming model/tools/max-turn fallback chains remain deterministic, unknown keys warn and are ignored, and preserving test evidence that unknown keys do not silently mutate behavior.
Step: guard local presets and Toolkit settings by persisting them locally only as non-authoritative convenience state and confirming presets cannot override governance enforcement or project truth.
Step: guard drafts and attachment selections by persisting them locally per root/persona/mode, dropping malformed records, and warning on storage failures without breaking chat.

Step: prepare permission-mode integration by mapping Toolkit mode controls to permission policy modes once the policy engine exists, marking enforcement TBD until accepted enums/contracts are available.
Step: check professional and project-truth boundaries, confirming UI copy, tests, and implementation do not imply local state, presets, drafts, or agent outputs are approved project truth.

Verification: pane keyboard resize/collapse check expects focusable resize handles, working keyboard resize where implemented, Home collapse, and End expand.
Verification: pane state persistence check expects width/collapse state to persist locally and remain non-authoritative.
Verification: Toolkit option controls check expects the UI to expose only supported per-turn options or mark unsupported items unavailable/TBD.
Verification: deterministic option handoff check expects runtime to receive supported options, deterministic fallback, and unknown keys warned and ignored.
Verification: local preset authority check expects presets not to write project truth and not to override governance enforcement.
Verification: draft/attachment local persistence check expects records keyed per root/persona/mode, malformed records dropped, and storage failures warned without breaking chat.
Verification: permission-mode controls check expects controls to map to enforced modes if the policy engine exists, otherwise enforcement remains clearly TBD.

Records to be produced for DEL-02-04 include Toolkit controls notes, pane resize/collapse notes, draft/preset storage guard tests, option-handoff tests, accessibility checks, local-state non-authority tests, policy-mode mapping evidence, and the PRD hash ruling, all currently TBD.

Specification scope: DEL-02-04 covers the UX/UI slice exposing runtime options and preserving pane layout, chat drafts, attachment selections, and local presets as non-authoritative convenience state for the Chirality desktop shell.
Included in scope: Toolkit controls for per-turn runtime options.
Included in scope: local pane resize/collapse state for File Tree, Toolkit, and Chat panes.
Included in scope: local draft, attachment-selection, and preset persistence guards.
Included in scope: UI behavior that respects deterministic runtime option fallback and warnings.
Excluded from scope: runtime engine internals.
Excluded from scope: SDK-specific option builder implementation, except where the UI must not contradict accepted runtime option behavior.
Excluded from scope: API key entry/status UI, secure-storage feedback, and typed runtime error display, which are assigned to DEL-02-05.
Excluded from scope: dependency extraction; this run intentionally does not create Dependencies.csv.
DEL-02-04-REQ-001: the shell shall support resizable and collapsible File Tree, Toolkit, and Chat panes.
DEL-02-04-REQ-002: pane resize/collapse behavior shall support drag and keyboard operation, Home collapses, End expands, and widths are persisted locally.
DEL-02-04-REQ-003: the Toolkit panel shall expose per-turn options for model, tools, max turns, mode, persona, and governance metadata as supported by runtime.
DEL-02-04-REQ-004: Toolkit settings and presets shall persist locally and remain non-authoritative.
DEL-02-04-REQ-005: local presets shall not override governance enforcement or project truth.
DEL-02-04-REQ-006: chat drafts and attachment selections shall persist locally per root/persona/mode.
DEL-02-04-REQ-007: malformed local draft or attachment-selection records shall be dropped.
DEL-02-04-REQ-008: local storage failures shall warn without breaking chat.
DEL-02-04-REQ-009: Toolkit mode controls shall map to permission policy modes once the policy engine exists.
DEL-02-04-REQ-010: Toolkit mode controls shall not be treated as mere prompt hints when permission policy enforcement exists.
DEL-02-04-REQ-011: runtime option fallback chains represented or initiated by the UI shall remain deterministic.
DEL-02-04-REQ-012: unknown option keys shall be ignored with warnings and shall not silently mutate behavior.
DEL-02-04-REQ-013: UI visibility of an option shall be non-authoritative; governance and permission policy remain authoritative.
DEL-02-04-REQ-014: the UI shall preserve a professional, dense-but-readable interface for the shell surfaces.
